clue.text: Endless material about radical plays

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter of the cloth word is cut off
the shortened cloth word goes around the other piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: DAMASK is a patterned fabric; endless, it loses its K
R is a standard abbreviation for radical

explanation.surface: A critic sneers at tediously long, revolutionary stage works.
explanation.walkthrough: DAMAS(K) wraps around R after its first letter: D-R-AMAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dramas are works for the stage, so plays is a plain synonym.

clue.text: Arrange date for an Olympic event

blocks.note: to dress is to arrange, as in dressing a shop window or troops in line
a date or period of time, as in the Stone Age

explanation.surface: Someone fixes the day on which an Olympic event will be held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrange' looks like an anagram signal, but it is the synonym DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the equestrian discipline of trained horse movements, contested at the Olympic Games.

clue.text: Dashing around this beast may be troubling

blocks.clueFragment: Dashing around this beast may be troubling
blocks.note: surface reading: a careless gallop near an animal might unsettle it
setter's reading: HARING (dashing) placed around the three-letter beast makes HARASSING, which means troubling

explanation.surface: Rushing about near some animal could alarm it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works in reverse: find a beast which, put inside a word for dashing (HARING), gives a word for troubling. HAR-ASS-ING is harassing, so the beast is the donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a donkey, a beast of burden, so beast describes it generally.

clue.text: On camera I made new drink

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer, filmed, concocted a fresh beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: An americano is a coffee drink of espresso diluted with hot water.

clue.text: Bananas — excellent with marmite?

blocks.note: crack as an adjective means first-rate, as in a crack shot
a marmite is a French earthenware cooking pot

explanation.surface: A breakfast verdict: bananas are great with Marmite, the British yeast spread?
explanation.walkthrough: The capital-free 'marmite' is the French word for a cooking pot, not the yeast extract spread the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Bananas is slang for crazy, and crackpot as an adjective also means eccentric or mad.

clue.text: Music magazine — famous American one

blocks.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper or magazine
Time is a well-known American news magazine; one stands for another magazine

explanation.surface: A music magazine is compared with a famous American publication.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragtime is a syncopated style of piano music popular in America around 1900.

clue.text: Budget car initially has great deal

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the first letter of car
a heap is a great deal, as in heaps of time

explanation.surface: An advert boasts that an economy car comes with a terrific bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: Budget used as an adjective means low-priced, as in budget airline.

clue.text: Female abandons large puma for naughty bit of fun

indicators.note: the female abbreviation walks away, leaving the word after it shorter
naughty letters misbehave and refuse to stay in order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, before the female letter leaves it
F is the abbreviation for female, the letter that departs

explanation.surface: A female animal leaves a big cat in pursuit of some mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: F (female) leaves 'for', and the remaining OR is jumbled with LARGE PUMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A parlour game is an indoor party amusement such as charades, a light piece of entertainment.

clue.text: Troy, an ancient city, important in this country

blocks.note: t is the abbreviation for troy, as in troy weight
Ur is the ancient Sumerian city, a crossword favourite
key means crucial or important

explanation.surface: Troy, an ancient and important city, lies within this country.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: the ruins of Troy are in Turkey, which makes the definition fit the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey is the country where ancient Troy stood, so this country refers back to the clue's own setting.

clue.text: Some men have no time for Rugby

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken out of the word

blocks.note: men named Steven, used as a plural
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Some men simply can't be bothered with rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some men' is a set of men all called Steven; STEVENS loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is the seven-a-side version of rugby union, played as an Olympic sport.

clue.text: Is it sweet to celebrate a fast finish?

definitions.text: Is it sweet to celebrate a fast finish?

blocks.clueFragment: Is it sweet to celebrate a fast finish?
blocks.note: surface reading: is it nice to cheer a quick end to a race
setter's reading: the end of the Lenten fast, marked with a chocolate treat

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' means abstaining from food, not speedy: Lent's fast ends at Easter, celebrated with chocolate. 'Sweet' is a confection, not a nice thing.
explanation.definitionFit: An Easter egg is a chocolate confection given at Easter, the feast that ends Lent's period of fasting.

clue.text: Bloomer gets fearsome person beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means losing the head, so the first letter goes

blocks.note: a terror is a frightening person, as in a holy terror

explanation.surface: A slip results in a frightening figure being executed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bloomer is not a flower or loaf here but British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is an embarrassing mistake, so it is a synonym for a blunder or slip.

clue.text: Girl embraces very loud one at start of company do

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold inside, so the girl's name wraps around the rest
the start of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: Sue is a girl's name
fortissimo, the musical direction for very loud
I is the Roman numeral one
the first letter of company

explanation.surface: A woman hugs a noisy guest at the start of an office party.
explanation.walkthrough: SU(FF I C)E. 'Company do' reads as a party, but do is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To do in the sense of 'that will do' means to be enough, which is to suffice.

clue.text: Tree with scouts in worried relative

indicators.note: worried letters are agitated and fretted out of their order

blocks.note: a fir is a coniferous tree
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family member frets when scouts are stuck up a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A first cousin is a child of one's aunt or uncle, a kind of relative.

clue.text: Pick up note about show

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the note's name is read backwards

blocks.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
to prove something is to show it is true

explanation.surface: Someone collects a memo about a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick up' suggests collecting, but here it means getting better.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up is to recover or get better, as sales or health do, which is to improve.

clue.text: Gardener's hemp mixed with heroin makes one barking

indicators.note: things mixed are stirred together, losing their original order

blocks.note: taken as written, with the S of the possessive
taken as written
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A gardener's cannabis laced with heroin drives someone mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' suggests barking mad, but here it is literal: a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A German shepherd is a breed of dog, and a dog is one that barks.

clue.text: Something very good on Kindle to underline

blocks.note: first meaning: the best part of an event
second meaning: to mark a passage on an e-reader

explanation.surface: A recommendation that marking passages on an e-reader is a great feature.
explanation.walkthrough: Kindle is Amazon's e-reader, which lets readers mark passages in colour rather than set anything alight.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a noun for an outstanding moment and a verb for marking text to stand out.

clue.text: Youth showing support in front of Harry and his gran

indicators.note: being in front means this piece comes first, ahead of the rest

blocks.note: a tee supports a golf ball
to harry someone is to nag or pester them
Prince Harry's grandmother was Queen Elizabeth II, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A young person backs Prince Harry and his grandmother, the late Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry with a capital looks like the prince but is the verb to harass; 'his gran' still uses the prince, since his grandmother was the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is a young person, and a teenager is someone aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: Organise long gun with tear gas for something trooper might use?

indicators.note: to organise is to arrange things anew, putting them in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions to a soldier on the weapons to carry.
explanation.walkthrough: The trooper alludes to the idiom 'swear like a trooper', not to any weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong language is swearing, and to swear like a trooper is the idiom for using it heavily.

clue.text: Overturn trunk containing exotic dress to reveal gem

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one word goes within the other
overturning a down entry flips it, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a tree trunk cut down is a log
a sari is the draped garment of South Asia, exotic to a British setter

explanation.surface: Tipping over a suitcase full of foreign clothes uncovers a jewel.
explanation.walkthrough: LO(SARI)G, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A girasol is a fire opal, a gemstone with a reddish glow.

clue.text: England once again left beaten

indicators.note: something beaten is knocked about, so its letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: England has lost yet again, reads the sports headline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'England once again' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglia is the Latin name for England, used in historical and poetic contexts.

clue.text: Shelter's variable in a humble dwelling

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: A plus SLUM, a squalid house
y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: The quality of a homeless refuge varies in a poor house.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum means refuge or protection, as in political asylum, a kind of shelter.

clue.text: Nearly twenty five quid in ship's gold fund …

indicators.note: nearly means not quite whole, so the last letter is dropped
in places the shortened sum inside the ship abbreviation

blocks.note: SS is steamship
a pony is slang for twenty-five pounds; nearly, it loses its Y
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Almost twenty-five pounds of a ship's gold goes into a kitty, the start of a two-clue story.
explanation.walkthrough: A pony is British slang for £25. The ellipsis links to the next clue, whose 'one' is this ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To sponsor is to back financially, so fund as a verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Dust benches erected around start of evensong

indicators.note: erected in a down entry means set upright, so the seats read upwards
around places the turned word on both sides of the letter
the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: pews are church benches
the first letter of evensong

explanation.surface: A church cleaner sets up the pews before evening service.
explanation.definitionFit: To dust and to sweep are both cleaning actions, so dust is a near synonym.

clue.text: … and get to tip of England by means of one

indicators.note: 'tip of' keeps only the first letter of 'England'

blocks.note: something that gets to you annoys you, which is to gall
the first letter of England
on as in running on petrol, by means of it

explanation.surface: Continuing the treasure story: reach Land's End by sailing in a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' refers back across the ellipsis to the ship of the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon is a large sailing ship, so it is one of the ships mentioned in the linked clue.

clue.text: Vehicle leaves NW city to get fabric

indicators.note: the vehicle departs, so its letters are taken out of the city name

blocks.note: Carlisle is a city in north-west England
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A car departs a north-western city to pick up some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine smooth cotton thread, and also the material woven from it.

clue.text: It's harsh to hang one German — then another

blocks.note: to swing is slang for being hanged
ein is German for one
another German: G is the abbreviation

explanation.surface: It's cruel to execute a German, and then a second.
explanation.definitionFit: Swingeing means severe, especially of cuts or penalties, so harsh is a synonym.

clue.text: Ignoring the odds dislike class

indicators.note: ignoring odd-numbered positions keeps only the even letters

blocks.note: letters two, four and six of dislike

explanation.surface: Someone, against the odds, dislikes a social class.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilk means type or kind, as in people of that ilk, a synonym for class.

clue.text: Game making you love college after start of the working week

indicators.note: after places these pieces behind the abbreviated day

blocks.note: Mon is the short form of Monday
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a poly is a polytechnic, a type of British college

explanation.surface: A student's game is falling for college on a Monday morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Monopoly is the property-trading board game, one example of a game.

clue.text: One tends to fire person having puff after school

indicators.note: after puts this piece behind the school abbreviation

blocks.note: S is an abbreviation for school
a toker is someone who takes a drag on a joint

explanation.surface: A pupil caught smoking after school is a firebrand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tends to' looks like 'is inclined to', but it means looks after.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker is the person who feeds and tends a furnace or boiler fire.
